Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — Redwood inference (next steps & success criteria)

Hi Priya / Tom —

Thanks again for your time today. Great conversation and appreciate the clear context on the evaluation goals for FinServe. Per our demo, I wanted to send a short recap and a proposed POC plan so we can align on success criteria, timeline, and owners. I attached a one‑page POC outline and a checklist for your procurement/security teams.

Recap (from today’s demo)
- Goal: Validate that Redwood can serve low-latency credit decisioning prompts across 3 production request patterns while meeting per-request p95 latency < 250ms and reducing monthly per‑token cost vs current on-prem pipeline.
- Scope: 3 example routes (short text classification, multi-turn decision prompts, and embedding-based similarity lookups).
- Constraints: Data residency in us-east-1; need SOC2 evidence and encryption-in-transit & at-rest.

Proposed POC plan (4 weeks) — high level
1) Week 0 (kickoff) — align success criteria, sign simple POC SOW (no charge trial), finalize contacts (security, infra, product).
2) Week 1 (env & access) — spin up a sandbox tenant in Redwood Dedicated (dev region us-east-1), exchange test API keys, provide sample prompt sets, confirm network/security requirements.
3) Week 2 (integration) — integrate 3 routes, run baseline QPS tests, collect latency & cost telemetry.
4) Week 3 (evaluation) — run evaluation harness, compare p95 latency, per-token cost, and qualitative output parity on key prompts.
5) Week 4 (wrap & decision) — review results, handoff playbook for production rollout or recommend next steps.

Success criteria (please confirm):
- Technical: p95 latency < 250ms for short prompts at 50 RPS aggregated across routes; no more than 3% output-regression (as measured by evaluation prompts).
- Cost: >= 20% reduction in per-token inference cost vs your current baseline under comparable load.
- Operational: Verified observability (tracing + token-level cost) and ability to rollback to baseline model variant.

Owners / suggested points of contact
- Redwood AE (me): Marissa Cole — program/contract lead
- Redwood SE: Dylan Brooks — technical kickoff & integration
- Redwood Security: Dev Patel — SOC2 & encryption details (cc’d separately)
- FinServe: Priya Rao (Product) — POC sponsor; Tom Greene (Procurement) — procurement / SOW

Next steps (proposed)
- Please confirm the success criteria above (reply with any edits).
- Can we schedule a 30-min kickoff next Tue or Wed for the integration team? Dylan will propose slots.
- I’ll circulate a short POC SOW and the checklist for your security team.

Attachments: FinServe-POC-Outline.pdf, redwood_poc_checklist.xlsx

Thanks — look forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
